result.title: SoK: Rethinking Membership Inference in Tabular Machine Learning
result.summary: Membership Inference Attacks (MIAs) are currently the dominant approach to evaluating privacy in machine learning applications. Despite their significance, several concerns remain unexplored, particularly with regard to tabular data. Existing evaluations focus predominantly on high-dimensional datasets, leaving the privacy behavior of small-to-medium datasets unexplored. In this paper, we present a new taxonomy for MIAs and conduct a comprehensive study of the factors influencing vulnerability. We evaluate four distinct state-of-the-art attacks across diverse tabular datasets and model architectures. Our results show that datasets with higher class granularity and majority class percentage are more susceptible to MIAs. We further demonstrate that advanced MIAs are highly dependent on adversarial knowledge of the target model, while reference model-free attacks often achieve statistically comparable results. Most importantly, we show that records with unique signatures (single-outs) remain highly vulnerable, even when common defenses are applied. These findings indicate that current defenses reduce average leakage, but fail to adequately protect the most sensitive individuals.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文是对表格机器学习中成员推断攻击（MIA）的系统化梳理，提出新的攻击分类法，并在多类表格数据集与模型架构上评估四种攻击，分析类别粒度、多数类比例、攻击者知识等因素对隐私脆弱性的影响。
AI.relevance_reason: 主题为表格数据的隐私泄露评估与防御，既不涉及视觉或多模态推理，也没有状态表示、证据筛选、生成式推理或训练监督等可供借鉴的机制线索，与 LVR 研究主线缺少实质联系。
